content.value_statement: Optimization problems often involve competing goals, constraints, and unclear trade-offs. This skill guides pymoo setup, algorithm choice, Pareto analysis, visualization, and decision making.
actual_capabilities: Explains pymoo workflows for single-objective, multi-objective, many-objective, and constrained optimization.
Provides example patterns for NSGA-II, NSGA-III, GA, DE, PSO, MOEA/D, and SRES.
Shows how to define custom ElementwiseProblem classes with objectives, bounds, and constraints.
Covers Pareto-front visualization with scatter plots, parallel coordinates, petal diagrams, and related tools.
Includes guidance for benchmark problems, genetic operators, repair operators, and MCDM selection.
limitations: It does not prove that an optimization model matches real-world constraints or business goals.
It assumes the user can install pymoo and required scientific Python packages.
Example scripts may need local plotting support to display charts.
It focuses on pymoo 0.6.x concepts and may need updates for future API changes.

use_cases.title: Compare Engineering Designs
use_cases.description: Use NSGA-II or NSGA-III to evaluate trade-offs across cost, weight, efficiency, and feasibility.

use_cases.title: Tune Algorithm Parameters
use_cases.description: Select operators, population sizes, termination rules, and benchmark problems for repeatable experiments.

use_cases.title: Choose a Pareto Solution
use_cases.description: Normalize objectives, apply preference weights, and document why one trade-off solution was selected.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Starter Optimization
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the pymoo skill to set up a simple single-objective optimization. Recommend an algorithm, termination rule, and result checks for my objective: [describe objective].

prompt_templates.title: Build a Constrained Problem
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the pymoo skill to define a custom ElementwiseProblem with these variables, bounds, objectives, and constraints: [details]. Explain the constraint signs.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a Pareto Front
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the pymoo skill to compare NSGA-II results for this multi-objective problem: [details]. Suggest plots, normalization, and MCDM selection steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Many-Objective Study
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the pymoo skill to plan an NSGA-III experiment with [number] objectives. Include reference directions, benchmarks, metrics, and reproducibility checks.

output_examples.input: I need to minimize cost and emissions while meeting capacity constraints.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend a constrained multi-objective pymoo workflow, NSGA-II, feasibility checks, scatter plots, and preference-based selection.

output_examples.input: My five-objective optimization result is hard to interpret.
output_examples.output: The skill would suggest NSGA-III reference directions, parallel coordinate visualization, objective normalization, and a documented decision-making method.

output_examples.input: I want to benchmark a custom algorithm against standard problems.
output_examples.output: The skill would map problem families, termination settings, seeds, metrics, and comparison plots for repeatable pymoo experiments.

best_practices: Normalize objectives before MCDM when scales differ.
Set random seeds and record termination criteria for reproducible results.
Validate constraint signs before judging algorithm performance.
anti_patterns: Choosing NSGA-III for two objectives when NSGA-II is simpler and sufficient.
Selecting one Pareto solution without documenting preferences or trade-offs.
Increasing generations before checking model scaling, constraints, and duplicate handling.

faq.question: What is pymoo best for?
faq.answer: It is best for optimization problems with trade-offs, constraints, evolutionary algorithms, and Pareto-front analysis.

faq.question: Does this skill support single-objective optimization?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers GA, DE, PSO, CMA-ES, termination criteria, and best-solution extraction.

faq.question: Can it help with constrained problems?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains feasibility-first handling, penalties, constraint-as-objective methods, repair operators, and specialized algorithms.

faq.question: Which multi-objective algorithms are covered?
faq.answer: It covers NSGA-II, NSGA-III, MOEA/D, R-NSGA-II, RVEA, AGE-MOEA, and related selection guidance.

faq.question: Can it help choose one final solution?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes MCDM guidance using normalization, preference weights, compromise methods, knee points, and hypervolume contribution.

faq.question: Does it install or run pymoo automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. Users must manage local installation, data, and execution.
